sources.label: Federal Reserve Board, FOMC projection materials, September 16, 2026, Table 1
sources.quote: Memo: Projected appropriate policy path Federal funds rate 4.1 4.1 3.9 3.6 3.2 4.1–4.4 3.6–4.4 3.1–4.1 3.1–3.6 3.0–3.6 (June projection 3.8 3.6 3.4 3.1)

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board via FRED, Federal Funds Effective Rate (FEDFUNDS), monthly
sources.quote: 2022-12-01 4.10 / 2023-12-01 5.33 / 2024-12-01 4.48 / 2025-12-01 3.72 (Source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (US); Units: Percent)

note: Projection is the median participant view of the appropriate year-end federal funds rate under each participant's own policy assumption (columns 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029, longer run 3.2, which is not plotted because it has no year). These are estimates, not a commitment. The history line is the monthly effective federal funds rate for December of each year (Board of Governors via FRED; 2019 1.55, 2020 0.09, 2021 0.08 read from the same file), a different definition from the SEP's year-end target midpoint, so the join is approximate: December 2025's effective rate 3.72 versus the SEP's 4.1 for end-2026 follows the September 2026 hike to a 3.75-4.00 range (reported). The FRED file was read via WebFetch (direct curl failed); the Fed table was read from the Fed's own HTML page.

title: Global insurance premium growth (real, total)

sources.label: Swiss Re Institute, sigma No 2/2026 World insurance: Shock absorbers in a fragmenting world
sources.quote: We estimate total premium growth (life and non-life) of 1.3% in real terms (2025: 3.9%) before a modest recovery to 1.6% in 2027 and a return to the long-term trend of 2% thereafter

sources.label: Swiss Re Institute, sigma 2/2026 Figure 7 (real premium growth, total, non-life and life, 2023-2027F)
sources.quote: Real premium growth, total, non-life and life, 2023-2027F. Source: Swiss Re Institute

note: Real (inflation-adjusted) annual growth in global direct premiums, per Swiss Re Institute sigma 2/2026, not nominal premium volume or other publishers' (for example Allianz euro nominal) series. 2026 and 2027 are Swiss Re forecasts (estimates); 2023-2025 are Swiss Re's own estimates from Figure 7 of the same report, read from the chart's data labels in the PDF text. Insurance is not one of the fixed categories, so the panel uses Finance, the closest. Only three history years are published in Figure 7.

title: Netflix annual revenue and 2026 guidance

sources.label: Netflix Q3 2026 shareholder letter (SEC 8-K Ex. 99.1)
sources.quote: For 2026, we expect revenue of $51.1B (+13% year over year) and an operating margin of 31.5%.

sources.label: Netflix 10-K for FY2025 (revenues 2025, 2024, 2023)
Netflix 10-K for FY2023 (revenues 2023, 2022, 2021)

note: Company guidance, not an independent industry forecast: Netflix's own full-year 2026 revenue expectation from its Q3 2026 letter (it trimmed 2026 ad revenue to ~$2.7B vs ~$3B earlier; total is 0.2% below the prior range mid-point). USD billions; actuals are the 10-K figures in thousands divided by one million, shown to three decimals, no FX or inflation adjustment. Single streaming service, not the whole TV market; the projection is one point (2026) and no later years are given.

note: BLS covers film, television, stage and other productions together; it is not TV-only, and the OOH lists television broadcasting stations among employers. Jobs (number of workers). History joins the base-year employment shown in successive Occupational Outlook Handbook editions (read from Internet Archive copies of bls.gov); each edition re-estimates the base, so jumps between years can reflect method and classification changes, not only real change. The projection is BLS's 2034 figure, a single point; no intermediate years are published. This is workforce size, not industry revenue.
